name: Saves the Day
label: Equal Vision
lede: A New Jersey high school band wrote the blueprint for a decade of emo and pop-punk in an NYU psychology class, survived a van wreck and a major label that vanished a month after their album came out, and kept going with Chris Conley outlasting more than a dozen bandmates.

eras.title: Sefler, then Saves the Day
eras.text: A New Jersey band called Sefler played melodic hardcore through high school, renamed itself, and made a debut album on winter break. Equal Vision put it out the summer they graduated, and touring it cost the band most of its members.

years.h: Sefler forms in New Jersey with Chris Conley on bass and vocals
years.p: The band that becomes Saves the Day starts as Sefler, a four-piece with Chris Conley singing and playing bass.

years.h: Bassist Sean McGrath renames Sefler as Saves the Day
years.p: Sean McGrath gives the band its new name, Saves the Day. Chris Conley and drummer Bryan Newman are the constants.

years.h: Can't Slow Down is recorded over Chris Conley's winter break
years.p: Saves the Day cut their debut with producer Steve Evetts during Chris Conley's senior-year winter break, while the band are still in high school.

years.h: Can't Slow Down · Equal Vision EVR 42
years.p: Saves the Day's melodic hardcore debut. Sean McGrath took the title from Lionel Richie's 1983 album; it had sold 8,000 copies by the time the next record came out.

years.h: Saves the Day's first full US tour, with [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]]
years.p: Saves the Day's first full tour of the United States is with Boston hardcore band Bane.

years.h: The driver and the roadie join Saves the Day
years.p: Guitarist Justin Gaylord quits after the first tour and David Soloway, who used to drive the band around in high school, replaces him. Roadie Ted Alexander is simply handed a guitar.
years.xp: Sean McGrath, the only bassist on Can't Slow Down, was pushed out during the writing of the next album. Chris Conley heard Eben D'Amico in a local band and brought him in.

eras.title: Written in Psychology 101
eras.text: Chris Conley wrote Through Being Cool at NYU, and Equal Vision's staff couldn't stop playing it. The band dropped out of college to tour it, and it sold like nothing the label had seen. Then the van crashed.

years.h: I'm Sorry I'm Leaving: 500 copies of an acoustic Saves the Day
years.p: An Equal Vision employee suggested an acoustic record after hearing "Three Miles Down". Saves the Day's EP comes out mid-1999 on Immigrant Sun, 500 copies pressed.

years.h: Eleven days at Trax East, and Chris Conley loses his voice
years.p: Saves the Day record Through Being Cool with Steve Evetts in South River, New Jersey, pulling all-nighters. Conley's voice gives out and he needs two extra half-days to finish.
years.xp: Bryan Newman came close to a breakdown in the studio and called Evetts the guru of the whole thing. Conley had been listening to the Foo Fighters' The Colour and the Shape, Weezer's Pinkerton and Joni Mitchell's Blue.

q: the most important record that we did
years.h: Through Being Cool · Equal Vision EVR-54
years.p: Chris Conley wrote Saves the Day's second album at NYU, lyrics in Psychology 101 and guitar parts at Bryan Newman's apartment on 7th Street and 2nd Avenue. Its pop-punk turn becomes a template for a generation.
years.xp:
Alternative Press later argued it shaped [[Fall Out Boy|516cef4d-0718-4007-9939-f9b38af3f784]], [[My Chemical Romance|c07f0676-9143-4217-8a9f-4c26bd636f13]] and [[Taking Back Sunday|350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d]]. Patrick Stump put it in his ten records that changed his life, saying he wouldn't have been in Fall Out Boy without it.

Conley calls it the band's most important record. The release show was with [[The Get Up Kids|1b54e90c-638e-4fdd-a20e-4ab09db9fdaf]], [[At the Drive-In|7e13cd1c-0300-4d03-bd8e-5f86dd99d74f]] and Midtown.

years.big: Faces on the cover means selling out
years.h: Hardcore kids call Through Being Cool's cover a sellout
years.p: The glossy cover shows the five members of Saves the Day as outcasts on a couch at a high school party. Hardcore fans said putting their faces on it meant selling out.
years.xp: Equal Vision's Dan Sandshaw had worried it sent the wrong message, and Bryan Newman regretted it. The CD art shows [[Gabe Saporta|8f4ad807-3363-46d1-8b2a-93a02fe6eb22]] kissing his college girlfriend, and actor James Ransone is passed out on a couch on the back.

years.h: A van accident on the H2O tour nearly ends Saves the Day
years.p: On a spring 2000 North American tour with [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]], Saves the Day's van crashes, an accident Wikipedia says nearly ended the band. They rejoin the tour in Seattle.

years.h: The "Shoulder to the Wheel" video that Saves the Day hated
years.p: Shot in February at David Soloway's parents' house with director Darren Doan, the clip hits TV in April. Bryan Newman said the band hated it as soon as they saw it.

years.h: Through Being Cool nears 50,000 and Saves the Day sign to Vagrant
years.p: Nearly 50,000 sold, a huge number for Equal Vision. Saves the Day move to Vagrant Records, and Vagrant founder Rich Egan becomes their manager.

eras.title: Puppets, Conan, and a label that disappeared
eras.text: On Vagrant, Saves the Day got on late-night TV, opened for Weezer and Blink-182 and made a video with Muppet-style puppets. The jump to DreamWorks went the other way: the label was sold out from under them a month after the album came out.

years.h: Stay What You Are · Vagrant
years.p: Made with Rob Schnapf in Hollywood, Saves the Day's third album sells 14,970 in its first week and more than 120,000 by March 2002. "At Your Funeral" and "Freakish" land on MTV2.

years.h: Drummer Bryan Newman leaves Saves the Day for college
years.p: The last founding member besides Chris Conley goes back to school. Damon Atkinson of Hey Mercedes fills in.

years.h: Saves the Day on Conan, then on tour with [[Weezer|6fe07aa5-fec0-4eca-a456-f29bff451b04]]
years.p: After a December spot on The Late Late Show, Saves the Day play Late Night with Conan O'Brien and join Weezer's Hyper Extended Midget Tour.

years.h: Saves the Day go Muppet in the "Freakish" video
years.p: Saves the Day are replaced by Muppet-style puppets in the "Freakish" video, then spend May and June on the Pop Disaster Tour with [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]] and [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]].

years.h: "At Your Funeral" reaches No. 76 in the UK
years.p: Saves the Day's single charts in Britain, where they've been supporting [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]].

years.h: Guitarist Ted Alexander is fired from Saves the Day
years.p: Ted Alexander, the roadie who became a guitarist, is dismissed and Chris Conley takes over guitar. Pete Parada becomes the drummer.

years.h: DreamWorks drops In Reverie, then is sold to Interscope
years.p: Saves the Day's In Reverie enters the Billboard 200 at No. 27. Chris Conley says DreamWorks walked away within days, and after Interscope absorbed the label the band was dropped.
years.xp: Produced by Rob Schnapf, In Reverie was Conley's Beatles-leaning, harmonically trickier record. The single "Anywhere With You" went nowhere without label support, but the album still sold 150,000 by mid-2006.

years.h: Former bassist Sean McGrath dies at 28; Ups and Downs is dedicated to him
years.p: Sean McGrath, who played on Can't Slow Down and named the band, died of intestinal cancer after a two-year illness. Vagrant's B-sides collection Ups and Downs is dedicated to him.

years.h: Saves the Day build the Electric Ladybug studio in Chico, California
years.p: With no label, Saves the Day set up their own studio, the Electric Ladybug, in Chico.

eras.title: The trilogy
eras.text: Chris Conley wrote three albums as one arc, discontent, remorse, acceptance, and called it a therapeutic experiment. By the end, Saves the Day's line-up had turned over so completely that nobody but Conley had played on an earlier record.

years.h: Sound the Alarm, part one of the trilogy · Vagrant
years.p: Recorded in 2005 with no label, Saves the Day's fifth album comes out after they re-sign with Vagrant in January. Conley says it's the expression of discontent.

years.h: Pete Parada leaves Saves the Day for [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]]
years.p: After more than four years, drummer Pete Parada joins the Offspring. Durijah Lang of [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]] takes over and plays on Under the Boards.

years.h: Under the Boards, trilogy part two · Vagrant
years.p: Chris Conley's reflection-and-remorse chapter, released on Vagrant.

years.h: Chris Conley and David Soloway's [[Two Tongues|85bcd622-bad8-4dd7-b577-ff7f5c195852]] with Say Anything
years.p: Conley and Soloway form Two Tongues with Max Bemis and Coby Linder of [[Say Anything|ee90d1b3-a4e2-4d18-9092-111d856e7e7a]]; the self-titled album, cut at the Electric Ladybug, comes out in February.

years.h: David Soloway leaves; Arun Bali takes lead guitar
years.p: After more than a decade, guitarist David Soloway departs Saves the Day in March. Arun Bali replaces him in April.

years.h: Saves the Day's rhythm section leaves to focus on Glassjaw
years.p: Bassist Manuel Carrero and drummer Durijah Lang go back to [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]]. Rodrigo Palma takes bass and Spencer Peterson the drums.
years.xp: Peterson lasted until September 2010, when he left to join Black Cards, [[Pete Wentz|26cea341-dfab-483f-9cdb-8de82da81019]]'s electropop project. Claudio Rivera replaced him.

years.h: Daybreak ends the trilogy · Razor & Tie
years.p: After several delays, Saves the Day's acceptance chapter arrives. It's the first Saves the Day album on which no one but Chris Conley had played on an earlier record.

eras.title: Back to Equal Vision
eras.text: Saves the Day went direct to fans to fund the next record, toured Through Being Cool for its fifteenth birthday, and in 2018 made their ninth album for the label that started them.

years.h: Saves the Day crowdfund their eighth album on PledgeMusic
years.p: Saves the Day ask fans to fund the record, sending pledgers demos of "Ain't No Kind of Love" and a Christmas cover of "Baby Please Come Home".

years.h: Dennis Wilson becomes Saves the Day's drummer
years.p: Dennis Wilson replaces Claudio Rivera behind the kit.

years.h: Saves the Day, the self-titled eighth album
years.p: Saves the Day's fan-funded album, toured with [[Into It. Over It.|d308cde9-0e44-4fe0-986d-e4657b6e8b7c]] and Hostage Calm. The same month they play Through Being Cool front to back at a secret Brooklyn show.

years.h: Through Being Cool at 15, on tour with Say Anything
years.p: Saves the Day play Through Being Cool in full while [[Say Anything|ee90d1b3-a4e2-4d18-9092-111d856e7e7a]] play ...Is a Real Boy, with [[Reggie and the Full Effect|2bfce7d5-001d-4618-adc3-c57c30fb17e6]] doing Under the Tray. Equal Vision reissues the album on vinyl.
years.xp: The idea came from Max Bemis, who noticed his record turned ten the same year Conley's turned fifteen. The tour ran November 14 to December 21. Earlier that year Saves the Day supported [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]] in the UK.

years.h: 9: nine songs, Saves the Day's ninth album · Equal Vision
years.p: Announced with "Rendezvous" on August 14, Saves the Day's ninth record comes out on Equal Vision, twenty years after Can't Slow Down.

eras.title: Reckoning and return
eras.text: Claudio Rivera came back to the drums, then allegations against Chris Conley in 2021 brought a public admission from him and a statement from Equal Vision. By 2026 Saves the Day were back on big tours.

years.h: Claudio Rivera returns to Saves the Day's drum stool
years.p: Dennis Wilson leaves Saves the Day and Claudio Rivera, the drummer from 2010 to 2013, rejoins.

years.h: Chris Conley accused of sexual misconduct; he admits causing harm
years.p: A former fan accuses Chris Conley of sexual misconduct and abuse of power, including sending unsolicited nude photos. Conley admits to inappropriate missteps causing irreversible harm; Equal Vision says it is looking into it.
years.xp: In his statement Conley said he was truly ashamed and embarrassed by his behavior. Equal Vision said it was working to uncover what had happened.

years.h: Saves the Day join [[Taking Back Sunday|350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d]]'s fall tour
years.p: Taking Back Sunday announce Saves the Day and [[Thrice|244afcb7-fa9a-49b1-9aa6-0149512d1c52]] as support on their fall 2026 tour.

years.h: "Invader", with [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] of Quicksand
years.p: Saves the Day release "Invader" featuring Walter Schreifels of [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] and [[Rival Schools|c661021c-3a9f-49d2-948a-c7f357cb1c87]].
